title: Re-roll: choose the visual world for qwertic.xyz
question: New hand, clarity first. The roll assigned the API reference. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll again.

options.label: Reference: Qwertic, documented
options.lineage: the best API reference docs: sidebar, plain headings, examples beside the prose
options.thesis: Qwertic documented like a well-made API: plain sections, real examples, and a request panel that answers "hiring" or "project".
options.viewport: Left: a sidebar with Overview, Work, Stack, Tools, Contact. Centre: "Qwertic. AI engineer, full stack." with a two-line summary and Book a call. Right: an example panel where choosing Hiring or Project prints a short response of relevant facts and a contact action.
options.risk: Tips into the familiar "me.json" gimmick if the example panel says more than the prose; the prose has to carry the page.

raised.raise: The overview owns the first viewport with one statement and one action, surrounded by real empty space, not a wall of sections.
Rank is depth: the current work sits frontmost and brightest, and older work steps back in weight, not size.
Statuses print inline as words (live, in progress, shipped) instead of badges and chrome.
No state relies on colour alone; every status carries a word.

options.label: Olivetti: Qwertic, the typewriter company
options.lineage: Olivetti's Milan-era identity: Pintori posters, Lettera 22 catalogues
options.thesis: QWERTY is in the name. Qwertic presented the way Olivetti presented a machine: bold flat colour, clear captions, Italian design confidence.
options.viewport: A Pintori-style composition of coloured key shapes spelling QWERTIC, with a plain caption block: AI engineer, full stack. Remote from Milan. Book a call.
options.risk: The cream ground and red accent sit close to a familiar AI-generated look, and it could read as design nostalgia.

options.label: Pop record sleeve
options.thesis: Qwertic as a release: one saturated ground, a portrait, and four tracks, the four things he does.
options.viewport: A tangerine field, a portrait cropped at the chin, QWERTIC in a rounded logotype, and four track titles in the corner: AI features, Full stack, Agent tooling, Contact.
options.case: Fuses well on clarity, since a closed set of four is instantly readable. Loses on audience: it's too playful for hiring leads and needs a strong portrait.
options.risk: Pop kitsch, and it depends on a good portrait photo.

options.label: Fashion flagship
options.case: Loses on both counts: there's no imagery to carry it, and it's the artsy you ruled out.
options.kept: One statement per viewport, with space around it.

options.label: Silk colour chords
options.viewport: Colour lanes crossing a white field.
options.case: Loses on both counts: abstract, and the facts get lost.

options.label: Ikebana alcove
options.case: Loses on both counts: beautiful, but unrelated to the work.

options.label: Cracktro scroller
options.thesis: Depth as rank on a black void.
options.viewport: One still line over drifting layers.
options.case: Loses on both counts: hacker aesthetic, hard for recruiters.
options.kept: Depth as rank: the frontmost item outranks the rest.

options.label: Phosphor terminal
options.thesis: The site as a live transcript.
options.case: Loses on both counts: the classic developer cliché, close to AI hype.
options.kept: States print themselves as text, not chrome.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The clean developer portfolio, done with full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Name, one-line role, three project cards, contact.
canonCard.risk: Looks like everyone else's by design, which is the generic portfolio you ruled out.
